title: Cause, effect and purpose linkers
titleVi: Từ nối chỉ nguyên nhân, kết quả và mục đích
summary: because/since/as, therefore/consequently, to/so that — nói rõ nguyên nhân, kết quả và mục đích mà không lặp từ.
whyItMatters: Task 2 gần như luôn hỏi *why* và *what happens as a result*. Nếu bạn chỉ dùng `because` và `so`, phần giải thích sẽ mỏng và lặp. Band 7.5 cần phân biệt **nguyên nhân** (because, since, as, due to), **kết quả** (therefore, consequently, as a result) và **mục đích** (to, in order to, so that). Chọn sai loại từ nối là lỗi cấu trúc, không chỉ là lỗi từ vựng.

sections.heading: because, since, as: same meaning, different weight
body: All three introduce a **clause** and answer *why*. **Because** is the most direct and the only one that can stand alone as a fragment answer: *Why did it fail? Because funding was cut.*

**Since** and **as** are more formal and often imply that the reason is already known to the reader: *Since the data are incomplete, the conclusions must be cautious.* In an essay this tone is useful — it presents your reason as shared ground rather than a new claim.
When the reason is a **noun** rather than a clause, switch to **because of**, **due to** or **owing to**: *Owing to the shortage of teachers, class sizes increased.* none of these takes a clause.

examples.right: Because the sample was small, the findings cannot be generalised.
Since public transport is limited, many commuters depend on private cars.
examples.note: **since** presents the reason as known background.

examples.right: Due to a shortage of teachers, class sizes increased.
examples.wrong: Due to there was a shortage of teachers, class sizes increased.

sections.heading: therefore, consequently, as a result: marking the effect
body: These are **sentence adverbs**. They normally open a new sentence (or follow a semicolon), with a comma after: *The sample was small. **Therefore**, the findings cannot be generalised.*
They can also sit in **mid position** for a more formal, flowing style: *The sample was small and the findings **therefore** cannot be generalised.* This is common in academic journals.
**Thus** and **hence** are the most formal; **as a result** is the most explicit about causation; **consequently** often carries a negative tone. Avoid stacking two of them in one sentence.

rows: Consequently, trust in the council fell.
As a result, waiting times doubled.
The sample was small, so the results are tentative.

sections.heading: Purpose: to, in order to, so as to, so that
body: For a **purpose**, the default is **to + infinitive**: *The city built cycle lanes to reduce congestion.* **In order to** and **so as to** are more formal; **so as to** is useful when the purpose clause comes first: *So as to avoid delays, the works were scheduled at night.*
When the purpose needs its own subject, use **so that + clause** (often with *can/could/will/would*): *The council widened the pavement **so that** pedestrians could keep their distance.*
**For** takes a noun or an -ing form, and describes what something is **used for**, not a personal intention: *This fund is for research.* *A knife is for cutting.* Never write *for to reduce*.

examples.right: The government introduced subsidies to encourage solar installation.
The government introduced subsidies so that low-income households could afford panels.
examples.wrong: The government introduced subsidies so that low-income households can afford panels last year.
examples.note: Backshift when the main verb is past: **could**.

examples.right: So as not to disturb residents, the work was scheduled at night.
examples.note: Negative purpose: **so as not to** / **in order not to**.

sections.heading: Result: so … that and such … that
body: **so + adjective/adverb + that**: *The cost was **so** high **that** many families withdrew.* **such + (a/an) + adjective + noun + that**: *It was **such** a high cost **that** many families withdrew.*
With quantity words, use **so many / so much / so few / so little + noun + that**: *There were **so few** places **that** the waiting list grew.*
These structures are stronger than *therefore*: they present the result as a direct consequence of an extreme degree, which is exactly the rhetoric of a problem–solution essay.

examples.right: The rent was so high that key workers could no longer afford to live in the city.
It was such a rapid expansion that infrastructure could not keep pace.
There was so little consultation that residents rejected the plan outright.
examples.wrong: There was such little consultation that residents rejected the plan outright.

sections.heading: Cause chains in a Task 2 paragraph
body: The strongest paragraphs do not repeat *because … so … because*. They alternate **clause linkers** with **nominalisation**, turning the cause into a noun phrase: *The **introduction of tuition fees** led to a **fall in enrolment** among low-income students.*

Useful nominal patterns: *lead to*, *result in*, *give rise to*, *contribute to* (+ noun); *stem from*, *arise from*, *be attributable to* (+ noun). These carry cause–effect inside a single clause, which is more compact than two clauses joined by *because*.
A model sequence: a nominalised cause, a consequence, then a purpose clause explaining the policy response. Three sentences, three different grammatical resources — and no repetition.

examples.right: The expansion of private tutoring has contributed to widening achievement gaps.
Poorly designed housing gives rise to health problems later in life.
examples.note: **give rise to** is formal and evaluative.

examples.right: Rising commute times stem from decades of underinvestment in rail.
examples.note: **stem from** reverses the direction: effect first, cause second.

commonMistakes.wrong: Because of the traffic was heavy, I arrived late.
commonMistakes.right: Because the traffic was heavy, I arrived late. / Because of the heavy traffic, I arrived late.
commonMistakes.why: **because of** đi với cụm danh từ; **because** đi với mệnh đề. Không trộn hai cấu trúc.

commonMistakes.wrong: The government built cycle lanes for to reduce congestion.
commonMistakes.right: The government built cycle lanes to reduce congestion.
commonMistakes.why: **for** không đi với *to + verb*. Mục đích dùng **to + infinitive**, hoặc **for + noun/-ing**.

commonMistakes.wrong: The cost was so high that many families withdrew, therefore the scheme failed.
commonMistakes.right: The cost was so high that many families withdrew. Therefore, the scheme failed.
commonMistakes.why: **therefore** là trạng từ nối câu, không phải liên từ. Cần dấu chấm hoặc chấm phẩy, không dùng dấu phẩy đơn.

commonMistakes.wrong: There was such little consultation that residents rejected the plan.
commonMistakes.right: There was so little consultation that residents rejected the plan.
commonMistakes.why: Với từ chỉ số lượng (**little, few, much, many**) dùng **so**, không dùng *such*.

commonMistakes.wrong: The council widened the pavement so that pedestrians can keep their distance last year.
commonMistakes.right: The council widened the pavement so that pedestrians could keep their distance.
commonMistakes.why: Mệnh đề chính ở quá khứ thì mệnh đề mục đích lùi thì: **could**, không phải *can*.

ieltsTips: Mở đoạn problem–solution bằng **nominalisation + cause verb**, rồi mới giải thích: ***The deregulation of rental markets** has **led to** a sharp **rise in** evictions.* Câu này dày thông tin hơn *Because the market was deregulated, evictions rose.*

Dùng **so that + could** để mô tả mục đích của một chính sách trong quá khứ: *The city pedestrianised the centre **so that** shoppers **could** move safely.* Đây là cấu trúc mục đích chính xác nhất khi chủ ngữ hai mệnh đề khác nhau.
Dùng **as a result** và **consequently** thay phiên nhau, mỗi đoạn tối đa một lần. Lặp *therefore* ba lần trong một bài là dấu hiệu band 6 về cohesion, dù ngữ pháp đúng.

Khi muốn nêu hệ quả mạnh, dùng **so … that** thay cho *very … therefore*: ***So few** landlords registered that the scheme became impossible to enforce.* Cấu trúc này tạo nhịp câu học thuật và nhấn đúng điểm cực đoan.

exercises.question: ___ the sample was small, the findings cannot be generalised.
exercises.explanation: A clause follows → **Because**. *Because of / due to / owing to* need a noun phrase.

exercises.question: The city built cycle lanes ___ reduce congestion.
exercises.explanation: Purpose with the same subject → **to + infinitive**.

exercises.question: The council widened the pavement ___ pedestrians could keep their distance.
exercises.explanation: A new subject (*pedestrians*) needs **so that + clause**.

exercises.question: There were ___ few places that the waiting list grew rapidly.
exercises.explanation: Quantity word *few* takes **so**: *so few places that*.

exercises.question: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
options: The cost rose, therefore demand fell.
The cost rose. Therefore, demand fell.
The cost rose therefore, demand fell.
The cost rose; therefore demand fell,
exercises.explanation: **therefore** opens a new sentence (or follows a semicolon) and takes a comma after it.

exercises.question: ___ to a shortage of teachers, class sizes increased.
The rent was ___ high that key workers could no longer afford to live there.
So as ___ disturb residents, the work was scheduled at night.
Rising commute times ___ from decades of underinvestment in rail.
The expansion of private tutoring has contributed ___ widening achievement gaps.
